```python
"""
LRU Cache Implementation

This module provides a thread-safe Least Recently Used (LRU) cache implementation
using only the Python standard library. It uses a combination of a doubly-linked list
(to maintain recency order) and a hash map (for O(1) lookups) to achieve O(1) time
complexity for get, put, and delete operations.

O(1) Operations Explanation:
- get(key): The hash map allows O(1) lookup of the node. Moving the node to the head
  of the linked list is O(1) because we have direct pointers to the node and its neighbors.
- put(key, value): If the key exists, we update the value and move the node to the head (O(1)).
  If the key is new, we create a new node, add it to the head (O(1)), and add it to the hash map (O(1)).
  If the cache is full, we remove the tail node from the linked list (O(1)) and delete it from the hash map (O(1)).

"""
LRU Cache Implementation

This module provides a thread-safe Least Recently Used (LRU) cache implementation
using only the Python standard library. It uses a combination of a doubly-linked list
(to maintain recency order) and a hash map (for O(1) lookups) to achieve O(1) time
complexity for get, put, and delete operations.

O(1) Operations Explanation:
- get(key): The hash map allows O(1) lookup of the node. Moving the node to the head
  of the linked list is O(1) because we have direct pointers to the node and its neighbors.
- put(key, value): If the key exists, we update the value and move the node to the head (O(1)).
  If the key is new, we create a new node, add it to the head (O(1)), and add it to the hash map (O(1)).
  If the cache is full, we remove the tail node from the linked list (O(1)) and delete it from the hash map (O(1)).
